ai.description: This large turtle reaches 56 cm. It features a high-domed, grey-brown shell and a grey head with bright red and yellow stripes. Males develop vivid red, yellow, and blue coloration during breeding.
ai.identificationRemarks: The Red-crowned Roofed Turtle is best identified by the striking, vivid red and yellow longitudinal stripes on the top of its head, which are absent in other *Batagur* species.
ai.habitat: The Red-crowned Roofed Turtle inhabits deep, flowing freshwater rivers with sandbars for nesting, primarily within the Gangetic plains at low to moderate altitudes.
ai.behavior: During the nesting season, females exhibit a unique behavior of returning to the same specific sandbanks annually to lay their eggs in deep, excavated nests.
ai.reproductionNotes: The Red-crowned Roofed Turtle is oviparous, nesting on sandbars from February to April. Females typically lay a single clutch of 11–30 eggs per season.
ai.distributionRemarks: The Red-crowned Roofed Turtle is endemic to the Ganges and Brahmaputra river systems, primarily occurring in northern India (Uttar Pradesh, Bihar, West Bengal) and Nepal.
